title: Apricot Bacon Pinwheels
description: Simple and elegant appetizers made with puff pastry, apricot preserves, cheese, and bacon.
author: Jackie
instructions: Preheat oven to 400° and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Thaw the puff pastry, shred the cheese, and cook and crumble the bacon.
Unfold the pastry and layer with preserves, mustard, cheese and bacon.
Roll up jelly-roll style and cut into 16 slices.
Place cut side down on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.
tips: Freeze Option: Freeze cooled appetizers in a freezer bag. To use, reheat on a parchment-lined baking sheet in a 400° oven until crisp.

title: Beef & Mushroom Braised Stew
description: A rich and savory beef stew braised with red wine, brandy, and herbs.
author: Jackie

ingredients.note: 1/4 tsp each of parsley, rosemary, sage, tarragon, thyme

instructions: Cut beef roast into 1-inch cubes, slice the mushrooms and onions, and mince the garlic.
Preheat the oven to 325°.
Sprinkle beef with salt and pepper.
In an ovenproof Dutch oven, heat oil over medium heat and brown the beef in batches.
Remove beef from the pan.
Add mushrooms and onions to the pan; cook and stir until tender.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute longer.
Stir in broth, wine, brandy, tomato paste and herbs.
Return beef to the pan and bring to a boil.
Bake, covered, for 1 hour.
In a small bowl, mix flour and water until smooth, then gradually stir into the stew.
Bake, covered, for 30 minutes longer or until stew is thickened and beef is tender.
Skim fat and serve the stew with mashed potatoes.
tips: Freeze Option: Freeze stew in freezer containers. To use, partially thaw in the refrigerator overnight. Heat through in a saucepan, stirring occasionally.

title: Chicken Tortilla Bake
description: A layered casserole with chicken, tortillas, and cheese, similar to an enchilada bake.
author: Jackie
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Grease a 13x9-in. baking dish. Shred the cooked chicken, finely chop the onion, shred the cheese, and warm the tortillas.
In a large bowl, combine the chicken, chilies, broth, soups and onion.
Layer half of the tortillas in the baking dish, cutting to fit if needed.
Top with half of the chicken mixture and half of the cheese.
Repeat the layers.
Bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes or until heated through.
tips: Freeze Option: Cover and freeze the unbaked casserole. To use, partially thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Let stand for 30 minutes before baking as directed, increasing time as necessary until a thermometer reads 165°.

title: Chickpea Curry
description: A simple and flavorful vegan curry made with chickpeas in a rich coconut-tomato sauce.
author: Jackie
instructions: Slice the onion, mince the garlic, and chop the cilantro.
In a large pot, heat the oil over medium-low.
Add the sliced onion, garlic, and crushed red pepper.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened and deep golden, about 15 minutes.
Increase the heat to medium.
Add the curry powder and cumin and stir until toasted, about 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and scrape the bottom of the pan to release any browned bits.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the chickpeas.
Stir, reduce to low heat, and let simmer until the sauce is thickened, about 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with lime wedges over rice or with naan.
tips: Add a tablespoon of water at a time if the onions get dry while cooking.

title: Chocolate Chip Cake
description: A rich and moist cake made with a yellow cake mix base, grated German chocolate, and chocolate chips.
author: Jackie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 325°. Lightly grease and flour a 10" tube pan or three 8" loaf pans. Finely grate the German chocolate bar.
Place the cake mix, pudding mix, milk, oil, and eggs in a large mixing bowl.
Blend with an electric mixer on low speed for 1 minute.
Stop the machine, fold in the grated chocolate, and scrape down the sides of the bowl.
Increase mixer speed to medium and beat for 2 more minutes, scraping the sides down if needed.
Fold in the chocolate chips until evenly distributed.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan(s), smoothing it out.
Bake for 58-60 minutes for a tube pan or 50-52 minutes for loaf pans, until golden brown.
Let cool in the pan on a wire rack for 20 minutes (tube) or 5 minutes (loaf).
Invert the cake onto a rack to cool completely, about 30 minutes more, before serving.
tips: Store cake covered at room temperature for up to 1 week.
To freeze, wrap in foil for up to 6 months. Thaw overnight on the counter before serving.

title: Creamy Chicken Enchiladas
description: Rich and creamy chicken enchiladas made with a savory soup and cheese sauce.
author: Jackie

ingredients.item: diced tomatoes with green chilies canned

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°. Grease two 13x9-in. baking dishes. Remove chicken from bones and shred. Cube the cream cheese and warm the tortillas.
In a large bowl, combine tomatoes, soups, milk and seasonings.
Transfer 3.5 cups of the mixture to another bowl and stir in the chicken and cream cheese.
Spread 1/4 cup of the plain soup mixture into the bottom of each baking dish.
Place 1/2 cup of the chicken mixture down the center of each tortilla.
Roll up the tortillas and place them seam side down in the baking dishes.
Pour the remaining soup mixture over the enchiladas and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake, uncovered, for 30-35 minutes until heated through.
Broil for 1-2 minutes until golden brown.
tips: Freeze Option: Cover and freeze unbaked casseroles for up to 3 months. To use, partially thaw overnight in the refrigerator and let stand for 30 minutes before baking. Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until 165°. Uncover and bake 5-10 minutes more until cheese is melted.

title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
description: Paleo-friendly chicken breasts in a creamy sauce with spinach, sun-dried tomatoes, and artichoke hearts.
author: Jackie
instructions: Mince the shallots and garlic; slice the sun-dried tomatoes.
Liberally season both sides of each chicken breast with salt.
Heat avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the oil is hot, place chicken breasts in the skillet and cook for 5 to 6 minutes per side, depending on thickness.
Once chicken is browned and firm, transfer it to a plate and set aside.
Clean any residue from the skillet, then return it to medium heat and add ghee or butter.
When melted, add the minced shallots and garlic. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, for about 30 to 60 seconds.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir well. Add the spinach, sun-dried tomatoes, and artichoke hearts.
Stir and allow the sauce to simmer until slightly thickened, approximately 5 minutes.
Return the chicken to the skillet and turn to coat in the sauce.
Serve warm.
tips: Serve with roasted potatoes, cauliflower rice, zucchini noodles, or spaghetti squash.

title: Creamy Tuscan Sausage Gnocchi
description: A one-pan meal featuring Italian sausage and potato gnocchi in a creamy sun-dried tomato and spinach sauce.
author: Jackie
instructions: Mince the garlic, grate the parmesan cheese, and remove sausage meat from its casings.
In a deep skillet, sauté the sausage over medium-high heat until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook for about 30 seconds.
Add the chicken broth, cream, lemon juice, sun-dried tomatoes, and gnocchi to the pan and stir.
Reduce the heat to medium, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir the gnocchi and add the spinach.
Cover the pan again for 1-2 minutes until the spinach has wilted.
Stir in the parmesan and basil (if using).
Season with salt & pepper to taste and serve immediately.
tips: There is no need to pre-cook the gnocchi; it cooks in the sauce.
If using oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drain the oil before adding them to the skillet.

title: Crispy Pork Carnitas
description: Pork carnitas made quickly in a Ninja Foodi, resulting in tender, juicy, and crispy meat.
author: Jackie
instructions: Chop the pork butt into 2-inch pieces. Cut the orange and onion in half. Peel and crush the garlic cloves.
Place pork, salt, oregano, and cumin in the Ninja Foodi pressure cook insert and combine well.
Squeeze the orange juices over the pork, then place the squeezed orange halves in the insert.
Add the onion, garlic cloves, and chicken broth.
Cover with the pressure cooker lid, set the valve to seal, and cook on High Pressure for 20 minutes.
Once complete, perform a quick release by switching the valve to vent.
When all pressure is released, open the lid and remove the orange, onion, and garlic cloves.
Set the Ninja Foodi to sauté on md:hi and allow the liquid to simmer and reduce for 10-15 minutes.
Close the Air Crisp lid, select Broil, and cook for 8 minutes until crispy.
tips: Use the crispy meat in tacos, bowls, sandwiches, or wraps.
Top with cilantro or any of your favorite toppings.

title: Frank's RedHot Buffalo Chicken Dip
description: The classic party dip featuring spicy buffalo sauce, chicken, and a creamy cheese blend.
author: Frank's RedHot
instructions: Shred the cooked chicken and soften the cream cheese.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl.
Spoon into a shallow 1-quart baking dish.
Bake for 20 minutes or until the mixture is heated through, then stir.
tips: Sprinkle with green onions and additional blue cheese if desired.
Serve with chips, crackers, and/or cut up veggies.

title: Homemade Chicken Noodle Soup
description: A comforting soup with homemade egg noodles, tender chicken, and vegetables.
author: Jackie
instructions: For the noodles, beat the egg and soften the butter. For the soup, chop the onion and celery, slice the carrots, mince the garlic, and shred the chicken.
To prepare the homemade noodles, stir together flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add the beaten egg, milk, and softened butter.
Knead dough until smooth, about 5 minutes, then let it rest in a covered bowl for 10 minutes.
On a floured surface, roll the dough out to 1/8 or 1/4 inch thickness.
Cut into desired lengths and shapes, then separate and allow to air dry.
For the soup, in a large pot over medium heat, melt 2 tablespoons of butter.
Cook onion, celery, and carrots in butter until just tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for an additional minute.
Pour in chicken broth and stir in the noodles, basil, oregano, poultry seasoning (if using), salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 15-20 minutes.
Stir in the shredded chicken and cook until heated through, then serve.
tips: For best results with homemade noodles, let them air dry for a couple of hours. If in a rush, 30 minutes will work.
Serve with peanuts, sriracha, and green onion for topping if desired.

title: Lentil Burger Lettuce Wraps
description: Hearty lentil and brown rice patties served in crisp romaine lettuce leaves with a fresh parsley-lemon hummus.
author: Jackie
instructions: Finely chop the onions and coarsely chop the carrots and celery.
In a food processor, combine onions, carrots, celery, tomatoes, ½ cup parsley, and 2 teaspoons garlic powder. Pulse until uniformly chopped.
Transfer to a large skillet and cook over medium-high for about 10 minutes until vegetables are tender and water has cooked off.
Add chili powder, then cook and stir for 3 minutes.
Stir in lentils, rice, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Cook about 10 minutes more until the mixture looks dry.
Remove from heat, let cool, then shape the mixture into patties using ½ cup per burger.
Place patties on a parchment-lined baking sheet and refrigerate for at least 1 hour until firm.
To make the hummus, combine chickpeas, the remaining ½ cup parsley, lemon juice, and the remaining ½ teaspoon garlic powder in a blender and blend until smooth.
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Bake patties for 20 to 30 minutes until heated through and lightly browned.
To serve, place each patty on 2 romaine leaves and top with the hummus.

title: Matzo Ball Soup
description: Classic Jewish comfort food featuring light and fluffy matzo balls simmered in a savory broth.
author: Jackie

ingredients.note: rendered chicken fat, coconut oil or vegetable oil

instructions: Finely chop the parsley and grate the ginger.
In a large bowl, combine the eggs, schmaltz, stock, matzo meal, nutmeg, ginger and parsley.
Season with 1 teaspoon salt and a few grinds of pepper. Gently mix with a whisk or spoon.
Cover and refrigerate until chilled, about 3 hours or overnight.
Fill a wide, deep pan with lightly salted water and bring to a boil.
With wet hands, take some of the mix and mold it into the size and shape of a Ping-Pong ball.
Gently drop it into the boiling water, repeating until all the mix is used.
Cover the pan, reduce heat to a lively simmer and cook matzo balls about 30 to 40 minutes.
tips: If desired, the cooked matzo balls can be transferred to chicken or vegetable soup and served immediately.
Alternatively, they may be placed on a baking sheet and frozen, then transferred to a freezer bag and kept frozen until a few hours before serving; reheat in chicken or vegetable soup or broth.

title: Mushroom Beef
description: A hearty beef stew with a rich mushroom flavor, perfect served over egg noodles.
author: Jackie
instructions: Cube the beef roast, slice the mushrooms, chop the carrots and onion, and mince the garlic and rosemary.
Bring broth and dried mushrooms to a boil in a large saucepan. Remove from heat and let stand for 15-20 minutes until mushrooms are softened.
Drain mushrooms, reserving the liquid. Finely chop the mushrooms and set aside.
Combine flour, salt and pepper in a bag; set aside 1 tablespoon for the sauce.
Add beef to the remaining flour mixture and shake to coat.
In a Dutch oven, brown the beef in oil in batches.
Add portobello mushrooms, carrots and onion; saute until onion is tender.
Add garlic, rosemary and rehydrated mushrooms; cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the reserved flour mixture until blended, then gradually stir in the reserved mushroom broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover and simmer for 1.5-2 hours or until beef is tender.
Combine cornstarch and cold water until smooth, then gradually stir it into the pan.
Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened.
Serve the stew with egg noodles if desired and top with blue cheese.
tips: Freeze Option: Freeze stew in freezer containers for up to 6 months. To use, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat in a Dutch oven.

title: Mushroom Sausage Strata
description: A savory breakfast casserole with sausage, mushrooms, and cheese, perfect for preparing overnight.
author: Jackie
instructions: Grease a 13x9-in. baking dish, cube the bread slices, and shred the cheeses.
In a large skillet, cook sausage over medium heat until no longer pink; drain.
Place the bread cubes in the prepared baking dish.
Sprinkle with the sausage, mushrooms and cheeses.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, cream, Worcestershire sauce and pepper; pour mixture over the cheese.
Cover the dish and refrigerate overnight.
Remove from the refrigerator 30 minutes before baking.
Preheat the oven to 350°.
Bake, uncovered, for 35-45 minutes or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.
tips: Freeze Option: After assembling, cover and freeze strata. To use, partially thaw in the refrigerator overnight. Remove from the refrigerator 30 minutes before baking. Preheat oven to 350° and bake as directed, increasing time as necessary.

title: Overnight Oats with Apple
description: Simple overnight oats with dates and raisins, served warm with fresh apple.
author: Jackie
instructions: Chop the pitted dates and dice half an apple.
In a container, combine rolled oats, plant-based milk, chopped dates, raisins, and cinnamon.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Heat the prepared oats in a pan or microwave with a splash of milk or water.
Serve topped with the diced apple and another sprinkle of cinnamon.

title: Parsley-Lemon Hummus
description: A fresh and zesty hummus made with parsley and lemon.
author: Jackie
instructions: In a blender or food processor, combine chickpeas, parsley, lemon juice, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Blend to a smooth paste, adding 1 to 2 tablespoons of water if needed to reach desired consistency.
tips: Serve with celery sticks.
Refrigerate leftover hummus in an airtight container.

title: Potato Burrito Bowls
description: A deconstructed burrito bowl featuring crispy potato wedges, black beans, rice, and a homemade salsa fresca.
author: Jackie
instructions: Cut the potato into 16 wedges, chop the tomato, finely chop the onion, and shred the romaine lettuce.
Preheat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place potato wedges in a steamer basket in a large saucepan with water just below the basket.
Bring to a boil and steam, covered, for 15 minutes until tender.
Transfer potatoes to a bowl, add taco seasoning, and toss to coat.
Spread the wedges in an even layer on the prepared baking sheet and bake for about 20 minutes until crispy.
For the Salsa Fresca, combine tomato, onion, lemon juice, cumin, and garlic powder in a blender.
Blend to a thick sauce, then add fresh cilantro and season to taste with salt and crushed red pepper.
To assemble, divide the potatoes, romaine, beans, rice, and corn among bowls and drizzle with the salsa.
tips: If preparing bowls in advance, store the components separately and wait to assemble until just before serving.

title: Sesame Chicken
description: A quick and easy stir-fry with sticky, sweet, and savory sesame sauce coating tender chicken.
author: Jackie
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 1/2 inch cubes. Grate the ginger, mince the garlic, and chop the spring onions.
In a medium bowl, combine the soy sauce, honey, sriracha, ginger, garlic, sesame seeds and sesame oil for the sauce.
In a large bowl, combine the chicken, cornstarch, salt and pepper.
Heat a large pan over high heat for at least 2 minutes, then add oil and chicken.
Stir-fry the chicken for 5-6 minutes until golden brown.
Add the sauce and simmer for 3-4 minutes until it becomes thick and sticky.
Serve with hot white rice, sprinkled with chopped spring onions and more sesame seeds if desired.

title: Spicy Mushroom Pasta
description: A quick pasta dish with a spicy tomato and mushroom sauce.
author: Jackie
instructions: Dice the garlic and bell peppers, and slice the mushrooms.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet.
Add garlic and cook for one minute, stirring often.
Add Thai chilis and stir constantly for 10-15 seconds.
Add bell peppers and cook for 3 minutes.
Add mushrooms and cook for 7-10 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, salt, pepper, and rosemary. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti.
Add the reserved pasta water to the sauce and bring to a simmer.
Add the cooked spaghetti to the sauce, along with red pepper flakes and parmesan cheese.
Toss to combine and serve immediately.

title: Tomato Mushroom Sauce
description: A simple and quick vegetarian pasta sauce with tomatoes, mushrooms, and spinach.
author: Jackie
instructions: Dice the onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Slice the mushrooms and tear the spinach into small pieces.
In a medium pot, sauté the onion and bell pepper for one minute.
Add the garlic and cook for one more minute.
Add the spices and toast for 1-2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and spinach, and let the sauce simmer for 8-10 minutes.

title: Shepherd’s Pie
description: A plant-based version of the classic comfort food, with a savory vegetable filling topped with mashed potatoes.
author: Jackie
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into large pieces. Coarsely chop the onion, carrots, and celery. Mince the garlic.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Place potato pieces in a steamer basket in a large saucepan with water just below the basket.
Bring to a boil and steam, covered, for about 20 minutes until tender.
Transfer potatoes to a large bowl, mash, and mix in 1 cup of milk, salt, and pepper. Set aside.
In a large skillet, combine the onion, carrots, celery, corn, garlic, Italian seasoning, and ¼ cup water.
Cook over medium-low for about 10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, process the rolled oats in a blender until they have a flour-like consistency.
In a small bowl, whisk the oat flour into the remaining 1 cup of milk.
Stir the flour mixture and vinegar into the skillet with vegetables. Cook until the mixture thickens.
Transfer the vegetable mixture to a 2-quart baking dish and top with the mashed potatoes.
Bake for 20 minutes until the potatoes are lightly browned. Let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Wonton Soup
description: A quick and easy soup with frozen wontons in a savory ginger and soy-infused broth.
author: Jackie
instructions: Mince the fresh ginger, chop the cilantro, and roughly chop the cashews.
Add the chicken broth, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sweet chili sauce, and ginger to a medium-large pot over high heat.
Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Add the wontons, frozen peas, and baby spinach.
Continue to cook over high heat for about 3 minutes until the wontons are warmed through.
Remove from heat and stir in cilantro.
Serve the soup garnished with chopped cashews.
tips: White vinegar can be used as a substitute for rice vinegar.

title: Vietnamese Pork Banh Mi
description: Crisp French baguette filled with savory marinated pork, pickled daikon and carrots, cucumber, fresh cilantro, and spicy jalapeño with seasoned mayo.
author: Jackie & Brandon
instructions: Marinate sliced pork with soy sauce, fish sauce, brown sugar, and minced garlic for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat with 1 tbsp oil. Sear marinated pork in batches until charred and cooked through (3-4 minutes per batch).
Slice baguettes lengthwise without cutting all the way through. Toast in a 400°F oven for 3 minutes until warm and crisp.
Mix mayonnaise with Maggi seasoning and spread generously inside both sides of each baguette.
Layer in charred pork, cucumber slices, pickled carrots and daikon, fresh cilantro sprigs, and sliced jalapeño peppers.
Press gently and serve immediately.
tips: Toasting the baguette creates the signature crunchy crust and soft, airy interior essential to authentic Banh Mi.

title: Lemongrass Chicken Banh Mi
description: Fragrant lemongrass chicken seared crisp, assembled in a warm baguette with crunchy pickles, chili crisp mayo, and fresh mint.
author: Jackie & Brandon
instructions: Toss chicken strips with lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, and honey. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Sear chicken in a hot oiled skillet for 6-8 minutes until golden and caramelized.
Split and lightly toast baguettes.
Spread spicy mayo on bread. Pack with hot lemongrass chicken, crunchy pickled vegetables, and fresh herbs.
tips: Chicken thighs remain juicy and tender under the high-heat char of the skillet.

title: Classic Philly Cheesesteak
description: Thinly shaved ribeye seared on a flat skillet with caramelized onions and melted provolone or Cooper sharp cheese on soft hoagie rolls.
author: Jackie & Brandon

ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Freeze ribeye for 45 minutes prior to prep so it can easily be sliced paper-thin across the grain.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté diced onions with a pinch of salt until golden and tender (about 8 minutes). Push to the side.
Turn heat to high, add remaining butter, and add the shaved ribeye. Season with salt and pepper.
Use two metal spatulas to chop and separate the meat as it sizzles and browns (about 3-4 minutes).
Mix the cooked onions into the beef and shape into 4 long portions matching the length of the rolls.
Place 2 slices of cheese over each portion of hot beef. Allow cheese to melt.
Open hoagie rolls and invert directly over the cheesy meat mounds. Use a spatula to scoop each sandwich off the griddle and flip upright.
tips: Thinly shaved ribeye cooks in just 3-4 minutes—do not overcook to ensure it stays succulent.

title: Quick Garlic Dill Pickles
description: Crunchy refrigerator dill pickles with fresh garlic cloves, mustard seeds, and whole peppercorns in a seasoned brine.
author: Jackie & Brandon
instructions: Wash cucumbers and slice into spears or rounds. Pack tightly into a clean 32-oz glass mason jar along with fresh dill, smashed garlic, peppercorns, and mustard seeds.
In a small saucepan, bring water, vinegar, salt, and sugar to a boil, stirring until dissolved.
Carefully pour hot brine into the jar, covering the cucumbers completely and leaving ½ inch of headspace.
Seal jar with lid, allow to cool to room temperature on the counter (about 1 hour), then transfer to the refrigerator.
Chill for at least 24 hours before enjoying.
tips: Refrigerator pickles stay ultra-crisp for up to 4 weeks in the fridge.

title: Traditional Red Pork Pozole
description: Deeply comforting Mexican stew with tender pork shoulder and white hominy simmered in a rich broth of rehydrated guajillo and ancho chiles.
author: Jackie & Brandon
instructions: In a large stockpot, cover pork cubes with 10 cups of water. Add onion quarters, halved garlic head, bay leaves, and 1 tbsp salt. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, toast dried chiles in a dry skillet for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Transfer to a bowl of boiling water and soak for 20 minutes to soften.

Blend softened chiles with 1 cup of soaking water, oregano, cumin, and 3 garlic cloves from the pot until completely smooth. Strain chile sauce through a fine sieve directly into the simmering soup pot.
Add drained hominy to the pot.
Simmer soup for another 45-60 minutes until pork is meltingly tender and broth is rich red.
Discard bay leaves and onion chunks. Adjust salt to taste.
Serve piping hot in deep bowls accompanied by shredded green cabbage, thinly sliced radishes, dried oregano, and fresh lime wedges.
tips: Pozole tastes even better the next day after the pork and hominy have absorbed the deep chile broth.

title: Vietnamese Vermicelli Noodle Bowl (Bun Thit Nuong)
description: Cool rice vermicelli noodles topped with charred marinated pork, crispy crushed peanuts, fresh herbs, pickled vegetables, and tangy Nuoc Cham dressing.
author: Jackie & Brandon

ingredients.item: Nuoc Cham sauce (fish sauce, lime, sugar, water, garlic, chili)

instructions: Marinate pork slices with lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, and brown sugar for 20 minutes.
Cook vermicelli noodles in boiling water for 3-4 minutes until tender. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Sear pork in a hot oiled grill pan or skillet for 5-6 minutes until charred on edges.
Divide cold vermicelli among four bowls over a bed of shredded lettuce and bean sprouts.
Top with charred pork, pickled carrots, fresh mint, cilantro, and crushed peanuts.
Drizzle generously with Nuoc Cham dressing just before eating and toss.
tips: Rinsing the cooked rice noodles in cold water halts the cooking and prevents them from becoming mushy or sticking together.

title: White Chocolate Cranberry Cookies
description: Soft and chewy bakery-style cookies studded with sweet white chocolate morsels and tart dried cranberries.
author: Jackie & Brandon
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and line two large baking sheets with parchment paper.
Whisk together flour, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In a stand mixer bowl, beat softened butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar until light and creamy (about 2 minutes).
Beat in eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla extract.
Gradually add the dry ingredients on low speed just until combined.
Fold in white chocolate chips and dried cranberries.
Drop rounded 2-tablespoon dough balls onto prepared baking sheets, spaced 2 inches apart.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until edges are golden and center is still slightly soft.
Cool on the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
tips: Underbaking slightly ensures cookies remain chewy and soft for days.
